prompts.flavor: Every war ends, the treaties promise. The deep has kept count, and it has room for a few more.
prompts.rules: Any named war, ancient or modern, legendary ones like the Trojan War included: civil wars, wars of independence and long rebellions all count. Battles, sieges, risings put down within weeks and wars of gods or fiction don't.

prompts.flavor: Kings fall, flags change, and the clocks are reset to Year One. The deep has seen every turning.

prompts.flavor: They built in stone so that someone would remember them. Something did.

prompts.text: Name a Prime Minister of Australia.
prompts.flavor: Thirty-one have held the office. One of them walked into the sea and did not come back.
prompts.rules: Anyone who has served as Prime Minister of Australia since 1901, including caretakers. Surnames are fine.

answers.lore: Australia's shortest-serving Prime Minister. He held the job for eight days in July 1945, between the death of John Curtin and the party's vote for Ben Chifley.

traps.reason: Led a party, or came close, but never became Prime Minister.
The "Father of Federation" was Premier of New South Wales, and died five years before there was a Commonwealth to lead.
Not a Prime Minister of Australia.

prompts.text: Name an Australian bushranger or outlaw.
prompts.flavor: They took to the bush with a stolen horse and a gun. Few of them saw thirty.
prompts.rules: Any bushranger, gang member or notorious outlaw of colonial Australia. Surnames are fine.

answers.lore: Escaped Macquarie Harbour in 1822 with seven other convicts and walked out of the Tasmanian bush alone, having eaten his companions. Then he did it again.
Often called Australia's only Chinese bushranger. He robbed travellers on the road near Mudgee in 1865 and was hanged at Bathurst that December.

traps.reason: Outlawed by the colony, but remembered as a resistance leader defending Country rather than as a bushranger.
An outlaw, but not one of ours.
A criminal of a later age. The bushrangers were gone by the 1900s.
Not a bushranger.
